## Review: v45 finalization candidate — PASS

I reviewed `finalize.py`, the `stopcheck.py` diff, `SKILL.md`/probe-prompt changes, and the test suite against the scoped spec. No must-fix correctness defects found in the five checked areas (real gate execution, deadline/receipt, before-after identity, Stop integration, standalone portability).

### Real gate execution
Confirmed via `test_actual_unchanged_gates_accept_canonical_contract_fixture` / `..._reject_broken_draft_...` / `..._blocks_unaccounted_state_...` — these run the actual `reportcheck/citecheck/statecheck/triagecheck.py` shipped tools against real fixtures, not stubs, and correctly reproduce a case where legacy Stop gates pass but the new `statecheck` catches an unreported service-install group. `parse_blocking` correctly matches run-bench.sh's "exit0 AND blocking0" rule, handles both `blocking`/`blocking_defects` keys, rejects bool-as-int, and tolerates leading diagnostic text before the JSON object.

### Deadline/receipt
Global deadline is shared and decremented across all four gates (`timeout = max(0.01, deadline - time.monotonic())`); a near-zero deadline still produces a metadata.json entry and stdout/stderr artifacts for every gate (verified by `test_deadline_leaves_incremental_receipt_for_every_gate`). `TimeoutExpired`/`OSError` are both caught and recorded as non-clean, never silently dropped.

### Exact before/after identity
`inputs_before/after`, `work_tree_before/after` (correctly excludes the `validation/` subtree so writing metadata.json mid-run doesn't self-invalidate the attempt), `evidence_before/after`, and `package_tree_sha256[_after]` are all compared; any mismatch sets `inputs_changed_during_validation` and forces `verdict: blocking`. Confirmed by `test_input_mutation_invalidates_an_otherwise_clean_attempt`.

### Stop integration
Recursion guard (`FINALIZE_STOP_ENV`) is checked before invocation and restored via `finally`; a failed finalize blocks Stop with a pointer to `work/validation/<attempt>`, never silently allows termination. Matches spec exactly.

### Standalone portability
Uses `sys.executable`, defaults `--package` to the skill root via `__file__`, no hardcoded interpreter/paths.

### Optional (non-blocking) limitations
- `tree_sha256`'s directory walk doesn't prune excluded paths (only filters files after listing), so it still walks/symlink-checks every prior `work/validation/<attempt>/` subtree on each run — a growing perf cost, not a correctness bug.
- If corpus/package content mutates during the internal read-consistency check inside `tree_sha256` (not the before/after comparison, but the per-file lstat-before/after-read guard), it raises an uncaught `ValueError`, producing a traceback exit instead of a structured `verdict: blocking` JSON line. Still fails safe (nonzero exit, evidence untouched), just less clean than the rest of the error handling.
- Single `work/worklist.tsv`/`rules.tsv` contract drops the old multi-host `--ledger` support — explicitly disclosed in the handoff doc, not hidden.

None of these are spec violations; they're worth a follow-up note but don't block this candidate.
